standard.title: Choreograph to communicate and challenge
standard.description: choreograph dance that communicates ideas, perspectives and/or meaning by selecting and manipulating elements of dance, choreographic devices and/or structure
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can choreograph dance by selecting and manipulating elements of dance and choreographic devices to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning (Y7-8, AC9ADA8C01). They have worked with binary, ternary and narrative structures, transitions, variation and contrast, and can document their process.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students choreograph dance that communicates ideas, perspectives and/or meaning by selecting and manipulating elements of dance, choreographic devices and/or structure.

nodes.label: Developing motifs and innovative manipulation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop movement motifs and manipulate elements and choreographic devices in innovative ways to communicate a clear choreographic intent.
nodes.minimum_width: Developing at least one movement motif; applying at least two forms of manipulation (e.g. addition, diminution, force, tempo) to generate material from the motif.
nodes.typical_width: Developing movement motifs and using choreographic devices or manipulating elements in innovative ways; experimenting with addition and diminution, force and tempo, different body parts; developing motifs from dances shared via social media or other sources; using style-specific forms to structure work.
wider: Develop motifs that synthesise influences from dances of different cultures, times and places — using respectful dance practice to adapt rather than appropriate
Use digital tools or social media-inspired movement (e.g. viral movement motifs) as starting points — manipulating these into original work that communicates a personal perspective
nodes.hinge_reason: Motif development and innovative manipulation are the compositional engine of senior dance. Without this, students produce choreography that is movement arrangement rather than genuine compositional craft — which limits expressive range and structural sophistication in the final work.

response_modes.reason: Innovative manipulation requires students to move beyond familiar devices — scaffold with explicit manipulation menus (addition, diminution, inversion, retrograde, fragmentation) and encourage systematic exploration before selection.
Students who develop motifs from diverse cultural influences and contemporary movement sources build wider compositional range and more personal choreographic voice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who develop motifs from diverse cultural and contemporary sources — and manipulate them across multiple structural frames — develop genuine compositional voice and can communicate complex, personal perspectives through dance.
success_criteria: Student can develop a movement motif and generate at least three variations using named manipulation techniques
Student can explain how the manipulation choices serve the choreographic intent

nodes.label: Structuring and communicating intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can structure a dance using elements, devices and/or choreographic forms — communicating ideas, perspectives or meaning with intentional structural choices.
nodes.minimum_width: A structured dance using at least one choreographic form or structural principle; clear communicative intent connected to structural choices.
nodes.typical_width: Choreographing dance that communicates ideas about identity, belonging or social justice; using and combining choreographic devices (addition, diminution, force, tempo); using style-specific forms; using Viewpoints to interrogate spatial and dynamic choices; adapting dance ideas from different cultural influences respectfully.
wider: Choreograph a dance that uses a culturally specific form (e.g. form associated with a specific cultural genre/style) — researching and applying it with appropriate cultural respect
Create a dance that takes a political position or advocates for a community — using structural choices to build argument or narrative

response_modes.reason: Structural communication integrates motif work (N1) with choreographic intent and audience relationship. Encourage students to test structural choices against their stated intent — 'Does this structure serve what you want to say?'

success_criteria: Student produces a complete dance with identifiable structural choices connected to communicative intent
Student can explain how at least two structural decisions serve the ideas, perspectives or meaning they intend to communicate

nodes.label: Documenting and reflecting on process
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can document their choreographic process — including analysis and evaluation of choices — and use this reflection to refine their work.
nodes.minimum_width: A brief documented record of choreographic process — at least two decision points noted with reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Documenting creative process in journals, blogs, video or audio recordings (with permissions); using Viewpoints to reflect on space, dynamics, intent; improvising and analysing movement choices to clarify choreographic intent; considering how emotion, political positions, critical theories shape their approach.
wider: Create a reflective portfolio documenting the full choreographic journey — including blind alleys, pivots and key insights
Use documented process to evaluate the relationship between intent and realised work — identifying the gap between what was planned and what was communicated

response_modes.reason: Choreographic documentation requires reflective writing and evaluation skills alongside artistic ones. Scaffold with specific reflection prompts — 'What decision did you make here?', 'What alternatives did you consider?', 'What influenced this choice?'

success_criteria: Student produces a process document recording at least two choreographic decisions with reasoning
Student can evaluate the effectiveness of at least one structural or element choice in communicating their intent
